messages.content:
How to generate a RESTful API request on Cisco Nexus Dashboard?
Version: 6.3.1
IP: 192.120.45.67
API name: get information of an interface
Parameter_fabricName: Network1
Parameter_nodeId: 12
Parameter_podId: 10
Parameter_interfaceType: Ethernet
Parameter_infoType: Speed

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Send a GET request to retrieve specified information for an interface from a network telemetry API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL endpoint to send the GET request to. This should include the base path without query parameters, e.g., 'https://{ip}/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo'.

params.description: The query parameters for the request.

fabricName.description: The name of the fabric to limit nodes pertaining to.

nodeId.description: The node identifier to limit results pertaining to.

podId.description: The pod identifier to limit results pertaining to.

interfaceType.description: The type of the interface to limit results pertaining to.

infoType.description: The type of information requested for the interface.

message.reasoning: We need to call the tool functions.requests_get with appropriate arguments. The user wants to generate a RESTful API request on Cisco Nexus Dashboard. They provide IP, version, API name, and parameters. We need to produce a GET request. The tool expects url: string, params: object. The url should include base path without query parameters, e.g., 'https://{ip}/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo'. So we need to construct that. The IP is 192.120.45.67. So url: 'https://192.120.45.67/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo'. Then params: {fabricName: 'Network1', nodeId: 12, podId: 10, interfaceType: 'Ethernet', infoType: 'Speed'}. But note interfaceType options: "gigabitethernet" | "fastethernet" | "ethernet" | "serial". Provided value is "Ethernet" but case-sensitive? Should be "ethernet". Also infoType options: "statistics" | "status" | "config" | "Speed". Provided "Speed" matches exactly? Options show "Speed" capital S. So keep as "Speed". But interfaceType should be lowercase "ethernet". We'll adjust accordingly. The tool will return some result. We need to output that. Let's call the tool.
